The International Court of Justice has found Myanmar responsible for committing genocide against the Rohingya, marking the first time the world's highest court has held a state liable for the crime.
The ruling follows years of investigations into mass killings, forced displacement, sexual violence and systematic discrimination against the Rohingya minority in Rakhine State. While the verdict is historic, major questions remain about enforcement, accountability and the prospects for the safe return of over a million Rohingya refugees.
